alt.en: A small printed page in German blackletter headed "Thalia." and "Zweytes Heft.", then "I. An die Freude." and an eight-line stanza beginning "Freude, schöner Götterfunken, Tochter aus Elisium", followed by a four-line "Chor" beginning "Seid umschlungen Millionen!"; at the foot, a printer's "A" and the catchword "Wem".
alt.es: Página impresa pequeña en letra gótica alemana, con el encabezado "Thalia." y "Zweytes Heft.", luego "I. An die Freude." y una estrofa de ocho versos que empieza "Freude, schöner Götterfunken, Tochter aus Elisium", seguida de un "Chor" de cuatro versos que empieza "Seid umschlungen Millionen!"; al pie, una "A" del impresor y la palabra de reclamo "Wem".

caption.en: An die Freude opening the second issue of Schiller's magazine Thalia (Leipzig: Göschen, 1786), the poem's earliest known printing, with the first-stanza lines on "der Mode Schwerd" and "Bettler werden Fürstenbrüder" that he changed in 1803.
caption.es: An die Freude al comienzo del segundo número de la revista de Schiller, Thalia (Leipzig: Göschen, 1786), la primera impresión conocida del poema, con los versos de la primera estrofa sobre "der Mode Schwerd" y "Bettler werden Fürstenbrüder" que él cambió en 1803.

source: Friedrich Schiller, ed., Thalia, vol. 1, Zweytes Heft (Leipzig: Georg Joachim Göschen, 1786), p. 1, "An die Freude"
licenceEvidence: The holder's IIIF record for Thalia (https://ds.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/viewer/api/v1/records/1944380/manifest/) gives "MD_USEANDREPRODUCTIONLICENSE": "Public Domain Mark 1.0" and "Access License Link": http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/. Printed 1786; Schiller died 1805 (see rights.md).

alt.en: The upper part of an engraved title page with flowing pen flourishes: the word "Sinfonie" in ornate blackletter set in a spray of flowers and leaves, then "mit Schluss-Chor über Schillers Ode: „An die Freude"" and, in script, "für grosses Orchester, 4 Solo- und 4 Chor-Stimmen,"; "(No. 9)" is pencilled at the right.
alt.es: La parte superior de una portada grabada con amplios trazos caligráficos: la palabra "Sinfonie" en letra gótica adornada, entre flores y hojas, luego "mit Schluss-Chor über Schillers Ode: „An die Freude"" y, en letra cursiva, "für grosses Orchester, 4 Solo- und 4 Chor-Stimmen,"; a la derecha, "(No. 9)" escrito a lápiz.

caption.en: The title of the score as Schott of Mainz published it in 1826, from a copy that may have been printed later from the same plates: a symphony "with closing chorus on Schiller's ode An die Freude", for large orchestra, four solo and four chorus voices.
caption.es: El título de la partitura tal como la publicó Schott, de Maguncia, en 1826, en un ejemplar que quizá se imprimió más tarde con las mismas planchas: una sinfonía "con coro final sobre la oda An die Freude de Schiller", para gran orquesta, cuatro voces solistas y cuatro de coro.

source: Ludwig van Beethoven, Sinfonie, mit Schluss-Chor über Schillers Ode An die Freude, 125tes Werk (Mainz and Paris: B. Schott's Söhnen; Antwerp: A. Schott; first published 1826, plate 2322), title page, upper part; this copy is pencilled "[185-?]" at the foot and shelved by the library under 1850
library: Boston Public Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)

Printed 1826 or in the 1850s either way; Beethoven 1770-1827; the engraver is unnamed. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: A wide printed page of music numbered 65, headed "Lock Hosp. Coll. (No. I.)" and "BONN. P. M. From Beethoven's Choral Symphony, (No. 9.) Adapted by E. I.", in four parts marked Soprano, Alto, Tenore and Basso on two systems, with four verses under the notes beginning "Head of the church triumphant, We joyfully adore thee".
alt.es: Página ancha de música impresa con el número 65 y el encabezado "Lock Hosp. Coll. (No. I.)" y "BONN. P. M. From Beethoven's Choral Symphony, (No. 9.) Adapted by E. I.", a cuatro voces marcadas Soprano, Alto, Tenore y Basso en dos sistemas, con cuatro estrofas bajo las notas que empiezan "Head of the church triumphant, We joyfully adore thee".

caption.en: Beethoven's tune as the four-part hymn tune BONN, "From Beethoven's Choral Symphony, (No. 9.)", on page 65 of Elam Ives's Mozart Collection of Sacred Music (New York, 1846), set to an older hymn whose second line is "We joyfully adore thee".
caption.es: La melodía de Beethoven como la melodía de himno a cuatro voces BONN, "From Beethoven's Choral Symphony, (No. 9.)", en la página 65 de la Mozart Collection of Sacred Music de Elam Ives (Nueva York, 1846), con un himno más antiguo cuyo segundo verso es "We joyfully adore thee".

source: Elam Ives, ed., Mozart Collection of Sacred Music (New York: Paine & Burgess, 1846), p. 65, "Bonn. P. M. From Beethoven's Choral Symphony, (No. 9.) Adapted by E. I."
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)

licenceEvidence: Published New York 1846 (Internet Archive record); Elam Ives died 1864; the words are Charles Wesley's (died 1788). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed book page numbered 332 with the running head "Songs of Hearth and Altar", the title "Hymn of Joy" and the line "To the Music of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony", then three eight-line stanzas beginning "Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee, God of glory, Lord of love".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con el número 332 y el título corrido "Songs of Hearth and Altar", el título "Hymn of Joy" y la línea "To the Music of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony", y luego tres estrofas de ocho versos que empiezan "Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee, God of glory, Lord of love".

caption.en: Van Dyke's "Hymn of Joy", "To the Music of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony", on page 332 of The Poems of Henry van Dyke (New York: Scribner's, 1911), with the first verse as we sing it, "Praising Thee their sun above".
caption.es: El "Hymn of Joy" de van Dyke, "To the Music of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony" (con la música de la Novena Sinfonía de Beethoven), en la página 332 de The Poems of Henry van Dyke (Nueva York: Scribner's, 1911), con la primera estrofa tal como la cantamos, "Praising Thee their sun above".

source: Henry van Dyke, The Poems of Henry van Dyke, Now First Collected and Revised (New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, 1911), "Songs of Hearth and Altar", p. 332, "Hymn of Joy"
